Mats come in several sizes, from lighter 3 x 8 foot sheets that one or two people can carry to 4 x 8 foot sheets and larger. Thicker, larger mats carry heavier loads but take more effort to move. Think about your heaviest regular machine, the gates and side yards you squeeze through, and how many mats you need to lay a path.

Ground protection mats for heavy equipment come with load ratings. Use them, and match the mat to the machine. Track mats work for tracked loaders and compact equipment, but check the rating before running heavy wheeled trucks across them.
If you only own a few mats, buy the size you can handle on every job rather than the biggest you can afford. Mats left in the truck because they are too heavy do not protect any lawns.

Plan the route before the equipment shows up. Lay mats on ground as level as you can, connect or overlap them so edges cannot kick up, and keep turns gentle. Sharp turns with tracked machines can scuff turf even through mats. Leapfrog mats forward as you go if the path is longer than your set.
When the job is done, pull the mats, rake out any flattened grass and hose the mats off before loading. Mud on a mat goes onto the next client's driveway otherwise.

On slopes, run the mats straight up and down where you can, and be careful when they are wet or icy. HDPE can get slick, and a loaded machine sliding sideways is dangerous. Keep ground workers clear of mats while equipment is moving on them, since an edge can flip up under a wheel.

Store mats flat or upright on edge so they do not warp. HDPE handles weather well, but long periods in hot sun on an uneven surface can distort them. Check connectors and edges for cracks. For a lighter, easier-to-handle option, see the 3 x 8 ground protection mats, and pair mats with outrigger pads for bucket truck setups.

faq.q: How much weight can ground mats hold?
faq.a: It depends on size and thickness. Check the load rating for each mat against your heaviest machine.

faq.q: Will ground mats damage grass?
faq.a: Short-term placement usually leaves grass flattened but intact. Avoid leaving mats down for days in hot weather, and turn machines gently.

faq.q: Can I use ground mats on pavers and driveways?
faq.a: Yes. Mats also help protect hardscape from outrigger and track damage.

name: Husqvarna Light Bars, 3/8" x .050"
title: Husqvarna Lightweight Chainsaw Bar, 3/8" x .050"
meta: A Husqvarna lightweight chainsaw bar in 3/8-inch pitch and .050 gauge. Less weight out front for felling and bucking. Fit, chain matching and care tips.
tagline: A lightweight 3/8" x .050" Husqvarna bar that takes weight off the front of the saw.
summary: A lightweight chainsaw bar takes weight off the front of the saw, which makes a real difference over a long day of felling and bucking. These Husqvarna light bars run 3/8-inch pitch chain at .050 gauge and suit mid to large saws.
highlights: Lighter than a solid bar of the same length
3/8-inch pitch, .050-inch gauge
Better balance for felling and bucking
Replaceable sprocket nose on most lengths

p: On a big saw with a long bar, most of the fatigue comes from holding weight out in front of you. A lighter bar moves the balance back toward the powerhead, so the saw feels quicker and is easier to hold level through a long bucking cut.
Lightweight bars give up some stiffness compared with solid bars, so they are best for felling and bucking rather than heavy prying or boring abuse.
That lighter feel also helps on storm work and firewood days, when you are making hundreds of cuts.
It also suits climbers bringing a larger saw aloft for a big removal cut.
Match the bar to your saw's mount and to the chain: 3/8-inch pitch, .050 gauge and the right drive link count for the bar length. Check the listing for mount and length before ordering.

Flip the bar each time you sharpen the chain, clean the groove and oil holes, grease the nose sprocket if it has a grease port, and dress the rails when they burr. Keep the chain sharp and tensioned. See more chainsaw bars.
Check rail height and the nose regularly. A lightweight chainsaw bar with spread or uneven rails will not keep the chain running straight, and a worn bar wears new chains quickly.

faq.q: Will this bar fit my saw?
faq.a: Check the mount type and length in the listing against your saw model, and use 3/8" pitch, .050" gauge chain.

faq.q: Are lightweight bars as strong as solid bars?
faq.a: They are strong for normal cutting but less stiff. For the hardest use, many cutters still prefer solid bars.

name: Husqvarna X-Precision Chainsaw Bar
title: Husqvarna Bar: X-Precision for X-Cut SP21G Chain
meta: The X-Precision Husqvarna bar pairs with X-Cut SP21G chain for a narrow, fast-cutting setup on compatible saws. Fit, chain matching and care basics.
tagline: Husqvarna's narrow-kerf bar for the X-Cut SP21G chain system.
summary: This X-Precision Husqvarna bar is built for the X-Cut SP21G chain, a narrow-kerf .325-inch mini pitch, .043-inch gauge system. The bar and chain combination takes less wood per cut, so a compatible saw cuts faster and uses less power.
highlights: Made for X-Cut SP21G chain
Narrow .043-inch gauge
Lightweight construction
Faster cutting on compatible saws

p: A narrower chain removes less wood with each pass, so more of the engine's power goes into cutting speed. The X-Precision system pairs a thin bar with Husqvarna's X-Cut SP21G chain to get that benefit on mid-size saws. For climbers and ground crews running compatible saws, the result is a quicker, smoother cut.
The tradeoff is that you must match the system. This bar only runs the matching .325 mini pitch, .043 gauge chain and a compatible sprocket.
It suits climbers and ground workers who want a lighter, faster-cutting setup on a mid-size saw.
It is also less tiring to carry aloft.
Before switching, compare the cost of the matched chain and sprocket as well as the bar.
Check that your saw is listed as compatible with X-Precision and confirm the length before ordering. Use the correct rim or spur sprocket.
Flip the bar regularly, keep the groove and oil holes clean, and dress the rails as they wear. Keep the chain sharp and correctly tensioned. See more chainsaw bars.

When the rails wear or the bar bends, replace it with another X-Precision bar rather than a standard one, so the narrow chain keeps running in a matched groove. Check the nose sprocket for roughness or play.
Store spare chain with the bar.

faq.q: Can I run regular .325 chain on an X-Precision bar?
faq.a: No. It is made for the narrower .043 gauge X-Cut SP21G chain.

faq.q: Which saws fit the X-Precision bar?
faq.a: Husqvarna lists compatible models for each bar. Check your saw before ordering.

name: Oregon Chainsaw Bar, .325" x .050"
title: Oregon Chain Bar, .325" Pitch x .050" Gauge
meta: An Oregon chain bar in .325-inch pitch and .050 gauge for mid-size saws. A dependable replacement bar for felling, bucking and storm work. Fit and care tips.
tagline: A replacement Oregon bar for .325" pitch, .050" gauge chain on mid-size saws.
summary: An Oregon chain bar is the go-to replacement when the original bar on a mid-size saw is worn, bent or pinched. This one runs .325-inch pitch chain at .050 gauge, a common combination on 40 to 60 cc saws.
highlights: .325-inch pitch, .050-inch gauge
Sprocket nose for low friction
Fits many mid-size saws (check mount)
Dependable replacement bar

p: Bars wear out. The rails spread or wear uneven, the groove gets shallow, and the nose sprocket goes rough. A bar that is pinched, bent or worn makes the chain cut crooked and wears out chains faster. When dressing the rails no longer fixes it, a new Oregon bar chainsaw setup brings the saw back to cutting straight.
Oregon also makes lightweight bar options in some sizes. If balance on a long bar matters to you, compare an Oregon lightweight bar with a standard one.
Oregon saw bars are made for a long list of saws, which is why they are a common stock item for crews running mixed fleets.
Order it with a fresh chain so the whole cutting system starts out matched and true.
Match the mount, length, pitch, gauge and drive link count to your saw and chain. Check the listing before ordering.
Flip the bar each time you sharpen, keep the groove and oil holes clean, grease the nose if it has a grease port, and keep the chain sharp. See more chainsaw bars.
A new bar deserves a new or fresh chain. Running a stretched, worn chain on a new bar wears the bar and sprocket faster.
Store spare bars flat and oiled.

faq.q: How do I know which Oregon bar fits my saw?
faq.a: Check your saw's mount, bar length, chain pitch, gauge and drive link count, then match them to the bar listing.

faq.q: Can I run .325 chain at .058 gauge on this bar?
faq.a: No. This bar is for .050 gauge chain. The gauge must match the bar groove.

name: Husqvarna PowerBox Carrying Case
title: Husqvarna PowerBox Chainsaw Carrying Case
meta: The Husqvarna PowerBox is a hard carrying case for a chainsaw and its kit. Keeps the saw protected and contained in the truck or shop. Fit and use tips here.
tagline: A hard Husqvarna case for transporting a chainsaw and its gear.
summary: The Husqvarna PowerBox is a rugged carrying case that holds a chainsaw and keeps it protected on the way to the job. It also keeps bar oil drips and sawdust contained, which matters if your saw rides in a car trunk or a clean truck bed.
highlights: Hard case for chainsaw transport
Protects the saw from knocks
Contains bar oil drips and sawdust
Carry handle for easy loading

body.h: Why carry your saw in a case
p: A loose saw in a truck bed gets bounced, scratched and sometimes cracked. Chains get dulled against tools and covers get broken. A case keeps everything in one place and protects the saw. The Husqvarna PowerBox also contains bar oil and fuel smells, so the saw can ride inside a vehicle without leaving a mess.
It suits homeowners and climbers who carry a saw in a car or SUV, and crews who want spare saws stored neatly.
The case also makes it easier to keep the saw and its scrench, file and spare chain together, so everything you need is in one place when you get to the job.
It is also a tidy way to keep a spare saw ready on the truck for a breakdown day.

Check the bar length and saw size the case fits before ordering. Always fit the bar cover and let the saw cool before putting it in the case. Empty the fuel tank for long storage or shipping, and secure the case so it cannot slide around.
See more chainsaw cases and scabbards, including the Husqvarna Classic case.
Clean out the case now and then, since sawdust and oil collect in the bottom and can mess up the next ride.
Keep it latched in transit.

faq.q: Will my saw fit in the Husqvarna PowerBox?
faq.a: Check the case's listed bar length and saw size against your saw before ordering.

faq.q: Can I put a hot saw in the case?
faq.a: Let it cool first, and always fit the bar cover.

name: The Classic Carrying Case by Husqvarna
title: Husqvarna Chainsaw Case: The Classic Carrying Case
h1: Husqvarna Chainsaw Case: The Classic Carrying Case
meta: The Classic Husqvarna chainsaw case keeps your saw protected, contained and easy to carry. Saw fit, what goes inside, and tips for transport and storage.
tagline: Husqvarna's hard plastic saw case for clean, protected transport and storage.
summary: The Husqvarna chainsaw case known as the Classic is a hard plastic carrying case that holds a saw with the bar attached. It protects the saw in transport, keeps oil and sawdust off everything else, and makes storage in the garage or shop neat and simple.
highlights: Hard plastic shell with carry handle
Holds the saw with bar and chain fitted
Keeps oil drips and sawdust contained
Stacks and stores neatly
Room for small items on most saw sizes

body.h: Why a case is worth it
p: Most saw damage does not happen while cutting. It happens in transport: the saw slides into a toolbox, the clutch cover cracks on a tailgate, the chain dulls against a jack. A hard Husqvarna saw case stops that. It also keeps bar oil from leaking onto the carpet of your SUV or the floor of the shop.
Many people buy a Husqvarna chainsaw with case for exactly that reason, and the Classic is the case they reach for when replacing a worn one or adding a case for a saw that came without.
It is also the simplest way to keep a saw in good shape between uses. A saw stored in a case stays cleaner, its controls are not knocked out of place, and the chain stays sharp until the next job.
Homeowners like the case for the same reasons: a clean garage, a protected saw and a simple way to keep the saw away from kids.

The Classic case is made for Husqvarna saws with the bar and chain fitted. Fit depends on the saw size and the bar length you run, so check the listing against your model before ordering. Larger saws and long bars may need a bigger case.

If you are not sure, measure your saw from the back of the handle to the tip of the bar and compare that with the case's interior length. A case for a Husqvarna chainsaw that is too tight forces the bar cover off or strains the latches.
If you run more than one saw, label the cases or keep each saw in its own color so the right saw goes out on the right job.

Always fit the bar cover before closing the case, even inside it. Let the saw cool after use. For long storage, run the tank empty or use stabilized pre-mix so the carburetor stays clean. Wipe sawdust off the saw first so it does not pack into the cooling fins.

In a vehicle, secure the case so it cannot slide or tip. Keep a scrench, spare chain and a file nearby so the case is a ready-to-go kit. For bucket work, a bucket truck chainsaw scabbard is a better fit, and the Husqvarna PowerBox is another case option.

Clean the inside of the case when bar oil builds up. Warm soapy water and a rag are enough. Check the latches and hinges now and then, since a latch that pops open in transit lets the saw slide out. A case that cracks is cheaper to replace than the clutch cover it was protecting.
Before storage, also check the chain for damage and touch it up with a file so the saw is ready when you open the case next.

faq.q: Does the Classic case fit all Husqvarna chainsaws?
faq.a: No. It fits a range of saw and bar sizes. Check your saw model and bar length against the listing.

faq.q: Can I store fuel in the case with the saw?
faq.a: Do not store fuel cans inside the case. Store fuel separately in an approved container.

faq.q: Is the case good for shipping a saw?
faq.a: It protects the saw well, but drain the fuel and follow the carrier's rules for shipping small engines.
